newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cargolux to keep B747-200Fs as new -400Fs arrive.
newsitem.headline: Cargolux to keep B747-200Fs as new -400Fs arrive.

text.p: Cargolux said strong growth in traffic and very buoyant market conditions had caused it to re-think the future composition of its freighter fleet.

"The arrival of two additional Boeing 747-400 freighters later this year (taking the overall number to five) (at first) put a question mark over at least one of our four 747-200Fs," Pierre Wesner, the carrier's vice- president for Europe, Middle East and Africa, told Reuters in a telephone interview from Luxembourg.
"But we have now decided to retain all of them because we estimate we'll need the capacity of nine, long-range freighters," he added.
The Luxembourg-based all-cargo airline flew 525 million freight tonne-kilometres (FTKs) in the first quarter of 1997, an increase of 14 percent on the same period last year.
This measurement is derived by multiplying the weight of cargo carried by the distance flown.
Strong growth in emerging markets such as Latin America aside, Wesner pointed to a recovery in traditional markets, like the Far East.
"Eastbound demand has grown considerably out of Europe, while the past few months have seen westbound demand recover after having been in the doldrums for several years," he noted.
Commenting on the North American market, Wesner said demand was very strong and stable.

In the Middle East sector, Cargolux had increased stopovers in Damasacus on an ex-Luxembourg service from one to two a week since the beginning of April as a result of growth in Germany-orginating freight, largely in the form of capital goods.
Cargolux had increased rates "almost everywhere" from April 1, by an average of close to 10 percent.
"This was in response to a positive demand situation and we are looking forward to a second round of increases in September or October 1997 as the market continues to stabilise," Wesner added.
